questions.e: 'are' appears in 467 and 639 → 6. 'green' appears in 467 and 485 → 4. So 'leaves' = 7.

questions.e: Each letter moves +2: W→Y, A→C, T→V, E→G, R→T. PAPER becomes RCQGT.

questions.e: A book is made up of pages; a wall is made up of bricks.

questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.e: A doctor works in a hospital; a teacher works in a school.

questions.e: Letters move back by 2 each time: R−2 = P.

questions.e: Apple, mango and banana are fruits; potato is a vegetable.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the odd one out — 121, 144, 169, 190:
questions.e: 121, 144 and 169 are perfect squares (11², 12², 13²); 190 is not.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the odd one out — Dog, Cat, Lion, Cow:
questions.e: Dog, cat and cow are domestic animals; the lion is a wild animal.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Pointing to a photograph, Ravi said, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' Who is she?
questions.e: Grandfather's only son is Ravi's father; his daughter is Ravi's sister.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A is B's brother. B is C's sister. C is D's mother. How is A related to D?
questions.e: A is C's brother, and C is D's mother, so A is D's maternal uncle.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If P is the father of Q, and Q is the sister of R, then P is R's:
questions.e: Q and R are siblings, so Q's father P is also R's father.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Rahul walks 5 km north, then turns right and walks 3 km. In which direction is he from the start?
questions.e: He ends 5 km north and 3 km east of the start — i.e. to the north-east.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A man faces east, turns left, then turns left again. Which direction does he face now?
questions.e: Facing east, a left turn faces north; another left turn faces west.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: All pens are books. All books are chairs. Conclusion: All pens are chairs.
questions.e: If all pens are books and all books are chairs, then every pen is a chair — the conclusion follows.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: Some cats are dogs. All dogs are animals. Conclusion: Some cats are animals.
questions.e: Some cats are dogs, and every dog is an animal, so those cats are animals — the conclusion follows.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: No birds are mammals. All bats are mammals. Conclusion: No bats are birds.
questions.e: Bats are mammals, and no mammal is a bird, so no bat is a bird.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Five persons A, B, C, D, E sit in a row. D sits at the left end, E at the right end, and B sits exactly between A and C. Who sits in the middle?
questions.e: Only B can be in the middle, with A and C on either side of it between the end positions D and E.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Five friends sit around a circle facing the centre. If P is to the immediate left of Q, Q is to the:
o: Second to the left of P
questions.e: In a circle, being immediately left of someone means that person is immediately right of you.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Which word cannot be formed from 'RAILWAYSTATION'?
questions.e: TRAINS, NATION and STATION can all be formed, but YAWNS needs a Y — RAILWAYSTATION has no Y.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If 'MOTHER' is written as 'REHTOM', how is 'FATHER' written?
questions.e: The word is simply reversed: FATHER → REHTAF.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Arrange in logical order: 1. Harvest 2. Sowing 3. Ploughing 4. Selling
questions.e: The farming sequence is ploughing → sowing → harvest → selling.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If 15th August was a Monday in a certain year, what day was 15th September of the same year?
questions.e: August has 31 days, so 15 Aug to 15 Sep is 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 days. Monday + 3 = Thursday.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: What was the day of the week on 26 January 1950?
questions.e: 26 January 1950 was a Thursday (India's first Republic Day).

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a row of 40 students, Ramesh is 12th from the left and Suresh is 15th from the right. How many students are between them?
questions.e: Suresh is 26th from the left (40−15+1). Between 12th and 26th: 26−12−1 = 13.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A clock shows 3:15. What is the angle between the hour and minute hands?
questions.e: Minute hand at 90°, hour hand at 90 + 15×0.5 = 97.5°. Difference = 7.5°.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: How many times do the hands of a clock coincide in 24 hours?
questions.e: The hands coincide 11 times every 12 hours, so 22 times in 24 hours.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If 8 workers build a wall in 10 days, how many days will 5 workers take for the same wall?
questions.e: Work = 80 worker-days. 5 workers take 80/5 = 16 days.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A train leaves at 6:00 AM and reaches at 2:30 PM covering 510 km. Its average speed is:
questions.e: Time = 8.5 hours. Speed = 510/8.5 = 60 km/h.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Venn diagram: 30 students like tea, 25 like coffee, 10 like both. How many like only tea?
questions.e: Only tea = tea total − both = 30−10 = 20.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a class of 50, 28 play cricket, 22 play football, 8 play both. How many play neither?
questions.e: At least one = 28+22−8 = 42. Neither = 50−42 = 8.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statement: All engineers are graduates. Conclusion: Some graduates are engineers. The conclusion is:
questions.e: If every engineer is a graduate, then at least those graduates who are engineers exist — 'some graduates are engineers' follows.

questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.e: Each term is multiplied by consecutive integers (×2, ×3, ×4, ×5); next is ×6: 120×6 = 720.

questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.e: 2, 3, 5 and 11 are prime numbers; 9 is composite.

questions.e: A is vertically symmetric, so its mirror image is identical; B, C, D change.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Water image: Which number looks the same in its water image?
questions.e: 8 is symmetric top-to-bottom, so its water image is unchanged; 6, 9 and 4 are not.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A large triangle is divided by 2 lines drawn from one vertex to the opposite side, forming 3 small triangles. How many triangles are there in total?
questions.e: The 3 small triangles combine: 3 singles + 2 doubles + 1 triple = 1+2+3 = 6 triangles in total.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A dice has 1 opposite 6, 2 opposite 5, 3 opposite 4. If 1 is on top and 2 faces north, which faces south?
questions.e: 2 faces north, so its opposite 5 faces south.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Two positions of a dice show 3 on top with 1, 2, 4, 5 around it. The number opposite 3 is:
questions.e: All four side faces 1, 2, 4, 5 are adjacent to 3, so the only number that can be opposite 3 is 6.

questions.e: P > R > Q, so P is the heaviest.

questions.e: Coal is characteristically black; snow is characteristically white.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If yesterday was Friday, what day is the day after tomorrow?
questions.e: Today is Saturday, tomorrow is Sunday, so the day after tomorrow is Monday.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: How many Mondays are there in February of a leap year if 1st February is a Wednesday?
questions.e: Leap-year February has 29 days = 4 weeks + 1 day. Starting Wednesday, Mondays fall on the 6th, 13th, 20th and 27th — 4 Mondays.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A shopkeeper's clock gains 5 minutes every hour. It shows 3:00 PM correctly at noon. What time will it show at 6:00 PM actual?
questions.e: In 6 real hours it gains 6×5 = 30 minutes, so it shows 6:30 PM.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statement: Some mobiles are costly. All costly things are electronic. Conclusion: Some mobiles are electronic.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If all Bloops are Razzies and all Razzies are Lazzies, then:
questions.e: Transitivity: Bloops → Razzies → Lazzies, so every Bloop is a Lazzie.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Which figure completes the pattern? A square is divided into 4 small squares; 3 are shaded. The missing pattern that makes rotational symmetry is:
questions.e: Shading the fourth square gives full 4-fold symmetry, completing the rotational pattern.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Odd one out in figures: circle, square, triangle, rectangle — which has a curved boundary only?
questions.e: Only the circle is bounded entirely by a curve; the rest have straight sides.

questions.e: Power is measured in watts (W); the joule measures energy and the volt measures potential difference.

questions.e: Velocity has both magnitude and direction, making it a vector; speed, distance and temperature are scalars.

questions.e: Uniform velocity means constant speed in a constant direction, so acceleration is zero.

questions.e: The first law states a body resists changes to its state of rest or motion — the law of inertia.

questions.e: The bullet's forward momentum produces an equal and opposite reaction on the gun — action and reaction.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.e: Newton's second law: the rate of change of momentum equals the applied force (F = ma).

questions.subject: Physics

questions.e: Orbiting astronauts and their spacecraft fall freely together, producing the sensation of weightlessness.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.e: Stored water's gravitational potential energy drives turbines that generate electricity.

questions.e: A dynamo (generator) converts mechanical rotation into electrical energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The speed of sound in air at 0°C is approximately:
questions.e: Sound travels at about 332 m/s in air at 0°C (about 343 m/s at 20°C).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Sound waves are:
questions.e: Sound propagates as compressions and rarefactions — longitudinal waves requiring a medium.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Ultrasonic waves have frequency:
questions.e: Ultrasound is defined as sound above the human hearing limit of 20 kHz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The pitch of a sound depends on its:
questions.e: Higher frequency is perceived as higher pitch; amplitude controls loudness.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.e: The ear distinguishes sounds 0.1 s apart; sound covers ~34 m round trip in that time, so the surface must be ~17 m away.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Light travels fastest in:
questions.e: Light attains its maximum speed, 3 × 10⁸ m/s, in vacuum; any medium slows it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The speed of light in vacuum is:
questions.e: c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s, a fundamental constant of nature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which colour of light has the longest wavelength?
questions.e: In the visible spectrum red has the longest wavelength (~700 nm) and violet the shortest.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rainbow is formed due to:
questions.e: Sunlight disperses into colours inside raindrops, reflects internally, and refracts out — forming the rainbow.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The image formed by a plane mirror is:
questions.e: Plane mirrors form virtual, erect images of the same size as the object.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A concave mirror is used in:
questions.e: Concave mirrors converge sunlight to a focus, making them ideal for solar furnaces; vehicle mirrors use convex mirrors.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The power of a lens is measured in:
questions.e: Lens power = 1/focal length (in metres), measured in dioptres.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.e: A concave (diverging) lens pushes the image back onto the retina in myopia.

questions.e: Parallel connection gives each appliance the full mains voltage and independent switching.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A fuse wire is made of an alloy of:
questions.e: Fuse wire is a lead-tin alloy with a low melting point so it melts and breaks the circuit on overload.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The device used to measure electric current is:
questions.e: An ammeter is connected in series to measure current; a voltmeter measures voltage in parallel.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.e: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure; the anemometer measures wind speed.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics

questions.e: The small edge area concentrates force into high pressure, cutting easily.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.e: Lower atmospheric pressure means water boils at a lower temperature on mountains.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Heat transfer in the absence of a medium occurs by:
questions.e: Radiation (e.g. solar heat) needs no medium; conduction and convection need matter.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The SI unit of temperature is:
questions.e: Kelvin (K) is the SI base unit of temperature.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.e: Silver has the highest electrical and thermal conductivity of all metals.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transformer works on the principle of:
questions.e: A transformer transfers energy between coils by mutual induction in an alternating magnetic field.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The Earth's magnetic north pole (toward which a compass needle points) is located near:
questions.e: A compass needle points toward the Arctic, where the Earth's magnetic north pole lies close to the geographic north pole.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following is a magnetic material?
questions.e: Nickel is ferromagnetic like iron and cobalt; copper and aluminium are not.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The photoelectric effect was explained by:
questions.e: Einstein's 1905 explanation of the photoelectric effect (light as photons) won him the Nobel Prize.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Nuclear fission was first achieved by:
questions.e: Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann discovered nuclear fission in 1938 (interpreted by Meitner and Frisch).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The half-life of carbon-14 is approximately:
questions.e: Carbon-14's half-life of about 5,730 years makes it useful for dating ancient organic material.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: X-rays were discovered by:
questions.e: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays in 1895, earning the first Nobel Prize in Physics.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The chemical symbol of gold is:
questions.e: Gold's symbol Au comes from the Latin 'aurum'. Ag is silver.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The chemical symbol of silver is:
questions.e: Silver's symbol Ag comes from the Latin 'argentum'.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The atomic number of carbon is:
questions.e: Carbon has 6 protons, so its atomic number is 6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of neutrons in C-14 is:
questions.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 14 − 6 = 8.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Electrons were discovered by:
questions.e: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron in 1897 through cathode-ray experiments.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The nucleus of an atom was discovered by:
questions.e: Rutherford's gold-foil experiment (1909) revealed the dense positive nucleus.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Neutrons were discovered by:
questions.e: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pH of a neutral solution at 25°C is:
questions.e: Neutral solutions have pH 7; below 7 is acidic and above 7 is basic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a strong acid?
questions.e: HCl dissociates completely in water, making it a strong acid; the others are weak acids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The chemical formula of washing soda is:
questions.e: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The chemical formula of baking soda is:
questions.e: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (sodium hydrogen carbonate), NaHCO₃.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Bleaching powder's chemical formula is:
questions.e: Bleaching powder is calcium oxychloride, CaOCl₂, used for disinfection.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Quick lime is chemically:
questions.e: Quick lime is calcium oxide, CaO, obtained by heating limestone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Slaked lime is chemically:
questions.e: Adding water to quick lime gives slaked lime, calcium hydroxide Ca(OH)₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The gas used in the manufacture of urea is:
questions.e: Urea is made by reacting ammonia with carbon dioxide; ammonia is the key nitrogen feedstock.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere is:
questions.e: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of air; oxygen is about 21%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The gas responsible for the greenhouse effect mainly is:
questions.e: CO₂ traps infrared radiation, driving the greenhouse effect; methane and water vapour also contribute.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ozone layer depletion is mainly caused by:
questions.e: CFCs release chlorine radicals that destroy stratospheric ozone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The hardest natural substance is:
questions.e: Diamond (10 on the Mohs scale) is the hardest known natural material.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Graphite is used in pencils because it:
o: Is a good conductor and soft
questions.e: Graphite's layered structure makes it soft enough to mark paper and electrically conductive.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Dry ice is the solid form of:
questions.e: Dry ice is solid CO₂, which sublimes directly to gas at −78.5°C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The metal that is liquid at room temperature is:
questions.e: Mercury is the only metal liquid at room temperature; gallium melts just above it (~29.8°C).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The most malleable metal is:
questions.e: Gold can be beaten into sheets just a few atoms thick — it is the most malleable metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The most ductile metal is:
questions.e: Gold is also the most ductile metal — a gram can be drawn into kilometres of wire.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Stainless steel is an alloy of iron with:
questions.e: Chromium (≥10.5%) forms the protective oxide layer; nickel adds corrosion resistance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Brass is an alloy of:
questions.e: Brass = copper + zinc; bronze = copper + tin.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Bronze is an alloy of:
questions.e: Bronze is primarily copper alloyed with tin.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Solder is an alloy of:
questions.e: Solder is a low-melting lead-tin alloy used to join electrical components.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The process of coating iron with zinc is called:
questions.e: Galvanisation coats iron/steel with zinc to prevent rusting.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Rusting of iron requires:
questions.e: Iron rusts (forms hydrated iron oxide) only when both oxygen and moisture are present.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The chemical formula of common salt is:
questions.e: Common salt is sodium chloride, NaCl.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Vinegar contains:
questions.e: Vinegar is a dilute (~5%) solution of acetic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Lemon and citrus fruits contain:
questions.e: Citrus fruits are rich in citric acid, giving them their sour taste.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Antacid tablets contain:
questions.e: Magnesium hydroxide (milk of magnesia) neutralises excess stomach acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The gas evolved when zinc reacts with dilute sulphuric acid is:
questions.e: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂↑; hydrogen gas is liberated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Photosynthesis produces:
questions.e: Plants convert CO₂ and water into glucose, releasing oxygen as a by-product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The periodic table was proposed by:
questions.e: Dmitri Mendeleev's 1869 periodic table arranged elements by atomic mass and predicted missing elements.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Modern periodic law is based on:
questions.e: Moseley showed properties repeat with atomic number, the basis of the modern table.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The lightest element is:
questions.e: Hydrogen (atomic number 1) is the lightest element.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Noble gases are placed in which group of the periodic table?
questions.e: Helium, neon, argon etc. occupy Group 18 (zero group) due to their full valence shells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The powerhouse of the cell is:
questions.e: Mitochondria generate ATP through respiration, earning the title 'powerhouse of the cell'.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Photosynthesis takes place in the:
questions.e: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which captures sunlight for photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The control centre of the cell is:
questions.e: The nucleus holds DNA and directs all cellular activities.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Protein synthesis takes place in the:
questions.e: Ribosomes read mRNA and assemble amino acids into proteins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The normal human body temperature is:
questions.e: Normal core body temperature is about 37°C (98.6°F).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The number of bones in an adult human body is:
questions.e: An adult human skeleton has 206 bones (babies have about 300).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The largest bone in the human body is the:
questions.e: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone in the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The smallest bone in the human body is the:
questions.e: The stapes (stirrup) in the middle ear is the smallest bone, about 3 mm long.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Red blood cells are produced in the:
questions.e: Red bone marrow produces red blood cells, white cells and platelets.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The lifespan of a human red blood cell is about:
questions.e: RBCs circulate for roughly 120 days before being recycled by the spleen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Haemoglobin contains the metal:
questions.e: Each haemoglobin molecule carries four iron atoms that bind oxygen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The universal blood donor group is:
questions.e: O− blood has no A, B or Rh antigens, so it can be given to almost anyone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The universal blood recipient group is:
questions.e: AB+ blood has all antigens and no antibodies against donor blood, so it can receive any group.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Blood clotting is helped by:
questions.e: Platelets (thrombocytes) aggregate at wounds and trigger the clotting cascade.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The largest organ of the human body is the:
questions.e: Skin is the largest organ by surface area and weight.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The largest internal organ of the human body is the:
questions.e: The liver is the largest internal organ, performing 500+ functions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Bile juice is produced by the:
questions.e: The liver produces bile, which is stored in the gall bladder and emulsifies fats.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Insulin is secreted by the:
questions.e: Beta cells of the pancreatic islets secrete insulin, which lowers blood sugar.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The enzyme that digests starch in saliva is:
questions.e: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) begins starch digestion in the mouth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Vitamin A deficiency causes:
questions.e: Vitamin A maintains the retina's photoreceptors; deficiency causes night blindness.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Vitamin C deficiency causes:
questions.e: Lack of vitamin C weakens collagen, causing scurvy (bleeding gums, fatigue).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Vitamin D deficiency causes:
questions.e: Vitamin D enables calcium absorption; deficiency softens bones, causing rickets in children.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Vitamin B1 deficiency causes:
questions.e: Thiamine (B1) deficiency causes beriberi, affecting nerves and the heart.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Vitamin K is essential for:
questions.e: Vitamin K is required to synthesise clotting factors II, VII, IX and X.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which vitamin is synthesised in the skin by sunlight?
questions.e: UV light converts a cholesterol precursor in skin into vitamin D3.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Malaria is caused by:
questions.e: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium, a protozoan spread by Anopheles mosquitoes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Tuberculosis is caused by:
questions.e: TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, a bacterium spread through the air.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: AIDS is caused by:
questions.e: AIDS is caused by HIV, a virus that attacks the immune system's T-cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Dengue is transmitted by:
questions.e: Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, which bite during the day, spread dengue.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Goitre is caused by the deficiency of:
questions.e: Iodine deficiency impairs thyroid hormone production, enlarging the thyroid gland.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The functional unit of the kidney is the:
questions.e: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons that filter blood and form urine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Exchange of gases in the lungs takes place in the:
questions.e: Tiny air sacs called alveoli provide the surface for oxygen–CO₂ exchange.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The part of the brain responsible for balance is the:
questions.e: The cerebellum coordinates movement and balance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The reflex actions are controlled by the:
questions.e: Reflex arcs pass through the spinal cord, enabling instant responses without the brain.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.e: Arteries carry oxygenated blood away from the heart (except the pulmonary artery).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The chamber of the heart that pumps blood to the body is the:
questions.e: The thick-walled left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood through the aorta to the whole body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following is a nitrogen-fixing plant?
questions.e: Pea (a legume) hosts Rhizobium bacteria in root nodules that fix atmospheric nitrogen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The process by which plants lose water as vapour is:
questions.e: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaves, mainly through stomata.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Stomata in plants are mainly found on the:
questions.e: Most stomata sit on the underside of leaves to reduce water loss while exchanging gases.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The female reproductive part of a flower is the:
questions.e: The pistil (carpel) contains the ovary, style and stigma — the flower's female parts.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Harappan site of Lothal is famous for:
questions.e: Lothal in Gujarat had a brick-built dockyard, evidence of Harappan maritime trade.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Mohenjo-daro is located in present-day:
questions.e: Mohenjo-daro lies in Sindh, Pakistan, excavated from 1922 by R.D. Banerji.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Great Bath was discovered at:
questions.e: The watertight Great Bath, likely used for ritual bathing, was found at Mohenjo-daro.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Vedas are written in which language?
questions.e: The four Vedas were composed in Vedic Sanskrit.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The oldest Veda is the:
questions.e: The Rigveda, a collection of 1,028 hymns, is the oldest of the four Vedas.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Gautama Buddha was born at:
questions.e: Buddha was born at Lumbini (in present-day Nepal) in 563 BCE.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Buddha attained enlightenment at:
questions.e: Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Buddha delivered his first sermon at:
questions.e: The Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta (first sermon) was delivered at Sarnath.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara, was born at:
questions.e: Vardhamana Mahavira was born at Kundagrama near Vaishali in 540 BCE.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The founder of the Maurya Empire was:
questions.e: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire around 321 BCE with Chanakya's guidance.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Arthashastra was written by:
questions.e: Chanakya (Kautilya), Chandragupta Maurya's minister, wrote the Arthashastra on statecraft.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the:
questions.e: The carnage of the Kalinga War (261 BCE) turned Ashoka toward Buddhism and non-violence.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Sarnath Lion Capital is associated with:
questions.e: Ashoka erected the Lion Capital at Sarnath; it is now India's national emblem.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Gupta ruler known as the 'Napoleon of India' was:
questions.e: Historian V.A. Smith called Samudragupta the Napoleon of India for his extensive conquests.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Iron Pillar at Mehrauli was erected during the reign of:
questions.e: The rust-resistant Iron Pillar inscription refers to King Chandra, identified as Chandragupta II.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Chinese traveller who visited India during Harshavardhana's reign was:
questions.e: Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) travelled across India during Harsha's reign (early 7th century CE).

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The founder of the Mughal Empire in India was:
questions.e: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat (1526), founding Mughal rule.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The First Battle of Panipat was fought in:
questions.e: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526, aided by field artillery.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought between Akbar and:
questions.e: Akbar's forces defeated Hemu at the Second Battle of Panipat in 1556.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Akbar's finance minister who introduced the Zabt revenue system was:
questions.e: Raja Todar Mal designed the Zabt (bandobast) land-revenue system under Akbar.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Taj Mahal was built by:
questions.e: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal at Agra in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Red Fort at Delhi was built by:
questions.e: Shah Jahan commissioned the Red Fort (Shahjahanabad) in the 17th century.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The last Mughal emperor was:
questions.e: Bahadur Shah Zafar (Bahadur Shah II) was exiled to Rangoon after the 1857 revolt.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Shivaji was coronated at Raigad in:
questions.e: Shivaji's coronation as Chhatrapati took place at Raigad in 1674.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Battle of Plassey was fought in:
questions.e: Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey on 23 June 1757.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Battle of Buxar was fought in:
questions.e: The British defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II at Buxar in 1764.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Revolt of 1857 began at:
questions.e: Sepoys mutinied at Meerut on 10 May 1857 before marching to Delhi.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Mangal Pandey was associated with the revolt at:
questions.e: Mangal Pandey's defiance at Barrackpore (March 1857) was an early spark of the revolt.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Rani Lakshmibai fought the British at:
questions.e: Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi was a leading figure of the 1857 revolt, dying at Gwalior in 1858.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by:
questions.e: Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, founded the Congress in 1885.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held at:
questions.e: The first Congress session met in Bombay in December 1885 under W.C. Bonnerjee.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Partition of Bengal was carried out in 1905 by:
questions.e: Viceroy Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905; it was annulled in 1911.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in:
questions.e: General Dyer's troops fired on a gathering at Amritsar on 13 April 1919.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in:
questions.e: Non-Cooperation began in 1920 following the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and Khilafat issue.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Chauri Chaura incident led Gandhi to:
questions.e: After the Chauri Chaura violence (February 1922), Gandhi called off Non-Cooperation.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Dandi March began on:
questions.e: Gandhi began the Salt March from Sabarmati to Dandi on 12 March 1930.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Quit India Movement was launched in:
questions.e: The Congress passed the Quit India resolution in Bombay on 8 August 1942.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: 'Do or Die' was the slogan of:
questions.e: Gandhi gave the 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro) call during the Quit India Movement.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Azad Hind Fauj (INA) was founded by:
questions.e: Rash Behari Bose founded the INA in 1942; Subhas Chandra Bose later took command and expanded it.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The slogan 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' was given by:
questions.e: Lal Bahadur Shastri coined 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' during the 1965 war.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: India's first war of independence is also called the:
questions.e: The 1857 uprising is called both the Sepoy Mutiny and India's First War of Independence.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The capital of British India was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi in:
questions.e: King George V announced the shift at the 1911 Delhi Durbar; the move completed in the 1920s.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Who wrote the national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana'?
questions.e: Rabindranath Tagore wrote 'Jana Gana Mana', first sung at the 1911 Calcutta Congress session.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: 'Vande Mataram' was written by:
questions.e: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote 'Vande Mataram' in his novel Anandamath (1882).

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Simon Commission arrived in India in:
questions.e: The all-British Simon Commission reached India in 1928 and faced boycotts with 'Simon Go Back' slogans.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The longest river of India is the:
questions.e: The Ganga (about 2,525 km) is India's longest river.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Ganga originates from:
questions.e: The Ganga rises at Gaumukh near the Gangotri glacier in Uttarakhand.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Brahmaputra is known as Tsangpo in:
questions.e: In Tibet (China) the Brahmaputra is called the Yarlung Tsangpo.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The longest peninsular river of India is the:
questions.e: The Godavari (about 1,465 km) is the longest river of peninsular India.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which river flows westward into the Arabian Sea?
questions.e: The Narmada flows west through a rift valley into the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The river known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' is the:
questions.e: The Kosi's frequent course changes and floods earned it the name 'Sorrow of Bihar'.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The river known as the 'Sorrow of Bengal' is the:
questions.e: The Damodar's devastating floods made it the 'Sorrow of Bengal' before the DVC dams.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The highest peak in India is:
questions.e: K2 (8,611 m) in the Karakoram is India's highest peak; Kanchenjunga is the highest within undisputed Indian territory.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Kanchenjunga is located in:
questions.e: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) stands on the Sikkim–Nepal border.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Western Ghats are also known as:
questions.e: The Western Ghats running along India's west coast are traditionally called the Sahyadri.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The highest peak of the Western Ghats is:
questions.e: Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala is the highest peak of the Western Ghats.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Aravalli range is located mainly in:
questions.e: The ancient Aravalli range runs across Rajasthan from Delhi to Gujarat.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
questions.e: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) passes through 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which state has the longest coastline in India?
questions.e: Gujarat has India's longest coastline (about 1,600 km).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The southernmost point of mainland India is:
questions.e: Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin) is the southern tip of mainland India; Indira Point is on Great Nicobar.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The northernmost state of India is:
questions.e: Ladakh is India's northernmost Union Territory since the 2019 reorganisation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The largest state of India by area is:
questions.e: Rajasthan (342,239 km²) is India's largest state by area.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The smallest state of India by area is:
questions.e: Goa (3,702 km²) is the smallest Indian state.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The state with the largest population (2011 Census) is:
questions.e: Uttar Pradesh had about 199.8 million people in the 2011 Census.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Chilika Lake is located in:
questions.e: Chilika, India's largest coastal lagoon, lies in Odisha.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The largest freshwater lake in India is:
questions.e: Wular Lake in Jammu and Kashmir is India's largest freshwater lake.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Sambhar Lake in Rajasthan is famous for:
questions.e: Sambhar is India's largest inland saline lake and a major salt source.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The monsoon winds that bring rain to most of India blow from the:
questions.e: The south-west monsoon (June–September) brings most of India's rainfall.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Mawsynram, the wettest place on Earth, is in:
questions.e: Mawsynram in Meghalaya's Khasi Hills receives the world's highest average rainfall.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The coldest inhabited place in India is:
questions.e: Dras in Ladakh, one of the coldest inhabited places on Earth, has recorded below −45°C.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Black soil is most suitable for growing:
questions.e: Moisture-retentive black (regur) soil of the Deccan is ideal for cotton.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Laterite soil is found mainly in:
questions.e: Laterite forms by intense leaching in high-rainfall areas like the Western Ghats.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Sundarbans are famous for:
questions.e: The Sundarbans mangrove delta is the largest habitat of the Royal Bengal tiger.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Kaziranga National Park, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, is in:
questions.e: Kaziranga in Assam protects the world's largest population of one-horned rhinos.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Gir National Park, home of the Asiatic lion, is in:
questions.e: Gir in Gujarat is the only wild home of the Asiatic lion.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The first national park of India was:
questions.e: Jim Corbett National Park (established 1936 as Hailey National Park) is India's oldest.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Palk Strait separates India from:
questions.e: The Palk Strait lies between Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Radcliffe Line is the border between:
questions.e: The Radcliffe Line demarcates the India–Pakistan (and India–Bangladesh) border.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The McMahon Line is the border between:
questions.e: The McMahon Line (1914 Shimla Convention) forms the boundary between India and China in Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The capital of Arunachal Pradesh is:
questions.e: Itanagar is the capital of Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The capital of Chhattisgarh is:
questions.e: Raipur is the capital of Chhattisgarh (formed in 2000).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which Indian city is known as the 'City of Lakes'?
questions.e: Udaipur in Rajasthan is famed for its lakes (Pichola, Fateh Sagar) and called the City of Lakes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Deccan Plateau is bounded by which two mountain ranges?
questions.e: The Deccan Plateau lies between the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Tea is mainly grown in India in:
questions.e: Assam and West Bengal (Darjeeling) are India's principal tea-growing regions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Green Revolution in India is associated with:
questions.e: M.S. Swaminathan led India's Green Revolution, built on Norman Borlaug's high-yield wheat varieties.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Constitution of India was adopted on:
questions.e: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949; it came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Constitution of India came into force on:
questions.e: The Constitution took effect on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly was:
questions.e: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee and is called the father of the Indian Constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The president of the Constituent Assembly was:
questions.e: Dr. Rajendra Prasad presided over the Constituent Assembly.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution begins with the words:
questions.e: The Preamble opens with 'We, the people of India…'.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which word was added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment?
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Fundamental Rights are enshrined in which part of the Constitution?
questions.e: Part III (Articles 12–35) guarantees the Fundamental Rights.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Right to Equality is covered under Articles:
questions.e: Articles 14–18 guarantee equality before law and equal protection of laws.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Right to Freedom is covered under Articles:
questions.e: Articles 19–22 protect freedoms of speech, assembly, movement and related rights.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Right to Constitutional Remedies is under Article:
questions.e: Article 32 gives citizens the right to move the Supreme Court to enforce Fundamental Rights.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which Fundamental Right was removed by the 44th Amendment?
questions.e: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the Right to Property from Fundamental Rights, making it a legal right under Article 300A.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Directive Principles of State Policy are in which part?
questions.e: Part IV (Articles 36–51) contains the Directive Principles.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Fundamental Duties are listed in:
questions.e: Article 51A lists the eleven Fundamental Duties, added by the 42nd Amendment.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The minimum age to become President of India is:
questions.e: Article 58 requires the President to be at least 35 years old.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The President of India is elected by:
o: An electoral college of MPs and MLAs
questions.e: The President is elected by an electoral college of elected MPs and MLAs (Article 54).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The term of the President of India is:
questions.e: The President holds office for five years (Article 56).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Who administers the oath of office to the President?
questions.e: The Chief Justice of India (or the senior-most judge) administers the President's oath.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio chairman of the:
questions.e: Article 64 makes the Vice-President the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The minimum age to become a member of the Lok Sabha is:
questions.e: A Lok Sabha candidate must be at least 25 years old (30 for Rajya Sabha).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is:
questions.e: Article 81 caps the Lok Sabha at 550 members (530 from states + 20 from UTs).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Rajya Sabha is a:
o: Permanent body not subject to dissolution
questions.e: The Rajya Sabha is permanent; one-third of its members retire every two years.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Money Bills can be introduced only in the:
questions.e: Article 109: Money Bills originate only in the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Who presides over a joint sitting of Parliament?
questions.e: Article 118: the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over joint sittings.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha was:
questions.e: Meira Kumar became the first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha in 2009.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Panchayati Raj was given constitutional status by the:

questions.e: Discount = 10% of ₹500 = ₹50, so the buyer pays ₹500 − ₹50 = ₹450.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A merchant wants at least his cost price of ₹800 on an article marked ₹1000. The maximum discount he can offer is:
questions.e: He can reduce the price by at most ₹200; as a percentage of ₹1000 that is 200/1000 × 100 = 20%.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: ₹5000 is deposited at 10% per annum compound interest. How much interest accrues in 2 years?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: On ₹8000 at 5% p.a. for 2 years, by how much does the compound interest exceed the simple interest?
questions.e: CI − SI for two years equals P(r/100)² = 8000 × 0.0025 = ₹20.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: What amount will ₹10000 grow to in 3 years at 10% p.a. compounded annually?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Find the compound interest earned on ₹2000 over 2 years at 20% per annum.
questions.e: First year: 2000 × 0.20 = ₹400; second year interest on ₹2400 = ₹480; total = ₹880.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: ₹4000 amounts to ₹4840 in 2 years at compound interest. The annual rate is:
questions.e: Growth factor = 4840/4000 = 1.21 = 1.1², so the rate is 10% per annum.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: ₹1500 is invested at 8% p.a. compounded half-yearly. What is the interest for one year?
questions.e: Half-yearly rate = 4%; amount = 1500 × 1.04² = ₹1622, so the year's interest is ₹122.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A sum of ₹6250 at 8% compound interest per annum yields what interest in two years?
questions.e: Amount = 6250 × 1.08² = ₹7290; subtracting the principal gives interest of ₹1040.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Rekha invests ₹10000 for 2 years at 10% p.a. compound interest. Her total interest income is:
questions.e: Amount after 2 years = 10000 × 1.21 = ₹12100; interest = ₹2100.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Two inlet pipes can fill a reservoir in 10 hours and 15 hours respectively. If both inlets are opened together, how long does the empty reservoir take to fill?
questions.e: Combined rate = 1/10 + 1/15 = 25/150 reservoir per hour, so time = 150/25 = 6 hours.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: One pipe fills a tank in 12 hours; a second pipe works twice as fast. How long do they take working together?
questions.e: The second pipe alone takes 6 hours; combined rate = 1/12 + 1/6 = 1/4 tank per hour, so 4 hours.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A cistern has an inlet pipe that fills it in 8 hours and an outlet pipe that drains the full cistern in 12 hours. With both pipes open, how long does the empty cistern take to fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/8 − 1/12 = 4/96 per hour, so the filling time is 96/4 = 24 hours.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: An inlet fills a tank in 6 hours; with an outlet also open, the empty tank fills in 8 hours. How long does the outlet take to empty the full tank?
questions.e: Let the outlet take x hours: 1/6 − 1/x = 1/8, so 1/x = 1/6 − 1/8 = 1/24 and x = 24 hours.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Two taps fill a tank in 12 and 15 hours; a third tap empties it in 20 hours. All three open together fill the empty tank in:
questions.e: Net rate = 1/12 + 1/15 − 1/20 = 360/3600 per hour = 1/10 per hour, so 10 hours.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A leak can empty a full tank in 24 hours. A pipe fills the tank in 8 hours. With the leak present and the pipe open, the empty tank fills in:
questions.e: Net filling rate = 1/8 − 1/24 = 1/12 of the tank per hour, so the tank fills in 12 hours.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: An express train cruises at 36 km/h. What is this speed in metres per second?
questions.e: To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18: 36 × 5/18 = 10 m/s.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A car moves at 54 kilometres per hour. Convert this speed to metres per second.
questions.e: To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18: 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Express a speed of 72 km/h in metres per second.
questions.e: To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18: 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Cycling to college at 40 km/h and returning by the same route at 60 km/h, what was the average speed for the round trip?
questions.e: Equal distances: average = 2×40×60/(40+60) = 48 km/h — less than the simple mean of 50 km/h.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A 240 m long train running at 72 km/h crosses a signal pole. How long does it take?
questions.e: Speed = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s; time = distance ÷ speed = 240 ÷ 20 = 12 seconds.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If CAT is coded as 24 (C=3, A=1, T=20; 3+1+20), then DOG is coded as:
questions.e: Add the alphabetical positions: D=4, O=15, G=7; 4 + 15 + 7 = 26.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Choose the odd one out:
questions.e: Apple, mango and banana are fruits; potato is a vegetable.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A person faces South, takes an about-turn. Which direction does he face now?
questions.e: Follow the turns in order: South → North, ending facing North.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, ?
questions.e: The differences are 4, 6, 8; the next difference is 10, so 20 + 10 = 30.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Which letter is 5th to the right of the 10th letter from the left in the English alphabet?
questions.e: The 10th letter from the left is J; 5 positions to its right is O (the 15th letter).

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Eight friends sit around a round table facing the centre. Clockwise from H the order is H, G, B, A, C, F, D, E. Who is sitting second to the left of H?
questions.e: Facing the centre, 'left' is the counter-clockwise direction. Two seats counter-clockwise from H is D.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a circle of eight seated facing the centre, the clockwise order starting at H is H, F, D, A, C, E, B, G. Who sits to the immediate right of A?
questions.e: Facing the centre, 'right' is the clockwise direction. The seat immediately clockwise from A holds C.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If 1 January 2026 is a Thursday, then 1 February 2026 is a:
questions.e: January has 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 days. Thursday + 3 days = Sunday.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a group of 50 people, 30 like tea, 25 like coffee and 10 like both. How many like neither?
questions.e: Like at least one = 30 + 25 − 10 = 45. Like neither = 50 − 45 = 5.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a group of 60 people, 35 like cricket, 28 like football and 12 like both. How many like neither?
questions.e: Like at least one = 35 + 28 − 12 = 51. Like neither = 60 − 51 = 9.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a survey of 100 people, 60 like Hindi, 55 like English and 25 like both. How many like only Hindi?
questions.e: Only Hindi = total liking Hindi − liking both = 60 − 25 = 35.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a survey of 80 people, 45 like bus, 40 like train and 15 like both. How many like only bus?
questions.e: Only bus = total liking bus − liking both = 45 − 15 = 30.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Pen : Write :: Knife : ?
questions.e: A pen is used to write; a knife is used to cut.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If CAT is written as XZG (each letter replaced by its opposite letter in the alphabet: A-Z, B-Y, C-X, …), then DOG is written as:
questions.e: Opposite letters: D→W, O→L, G→T, giving WLT.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If MANGO is written as NBOHP (each letter shifted one step forward), then APPLE is written as:
questions.e: Shift each letter one step forward: A→B, P→Q, P→Q, L→M, E→F, giving BQQMF.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A die is rolled so that 3 faces north and 5 is on top. On a standard die, which number faces south?
questions.e: South is opposite north. On a standard die opposite faces sum to 7, so opposite 3 is 7 − 3 = 4.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a certain code, '+' stands for '×', '−' for '÷', '×' for '+' and '÷' for '−'. Evaluate 12 ÷ 6 + 3 − 2 × 4.
questions.e: After substitution the expression reads 12 − 6 × 3 ÷ 2 + 4; applying BODMAS gives 7.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Suppose the symbols are redefined as: '+' means '−', '−' means '×', '×' means '÷' and '÷' means '+'. Find the value of 20 ÷ 4 − 3 + 8 × 2.
questions.e: After substitution the expression reads 20 + 4 × 3 − 8 ÷ 2; applying BODMAS gives 28.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If operators are interchanged so that '+' becomes '×', '−' becomes '+', '×' becomes '−' and '÷' remains unchanged, what is the value of 15 × 5 + 4 − 6 ÷ 2?
questions.e: After substitution the expression reads 15 − 5 × 4 + 6 ÷ 2; applying BODMAS gives -2.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Using the substitutions '+' → '÷' and '÷' → '+' (all other symbols keep their usual meanings), compute 36 + 6 ÷ 3 × 2 − 5.
questions.e: After substitution the expression reads 36 ÷ 6 + 3 × 2 − 5; applying BODMAS gives 7.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Which figure is the odd one out? (a) Square (b) Triangle (c) Circle (d) Rectangle
questions.e: Square, triangle and rectangle are all polygons made of straight line segments, while a circle is a curved figure with no straight sides.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the odd one out: (a) Cube (b) Cuboid (c) Cylinder (d) Sphere
questions.e: A sphere has a single continuous curved surface with no flat faces or edges, while the cube, cuboid and cylinder each have flat faces.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Which is different from the others? (a) Pentagon (b) Hexagon (c) Octagon (d) Oval
questions.e: Pentagon, hexagon and octagon are polygons with straight sides; the oval is a curved closed figure.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Odd one out: (a) Rhombus (b) Parallelogram (c) Trapezium (d) Cone
questions.e: Rhombus, parallelogram and trapezium are two-dimensional quadrilaterals, whereas a cone is a three-dimensional solid.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Pointing to a photograph, a man said, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the woman related to the man?
questions.e: The grandfather's only son is the man's father, and the father's daughter is the man's sister.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A woman introduces a man as 'the son of my mother's only daughter'. How is the man related to the woman?
questions.e: The mother's only daughter is the woman herself, so the woman's son is being introduced.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Ravi says, 'My mother's only brother's only sister is my mother.' How is Ravi related to the speaker's mother? He is her:
questions.e: The mother's only brother's only sister is the mother herself; the speaker says 'my mother', so Ravi is her son.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Anil said, 'Rani's mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is Anil related to Rani?
questions.e: The only daughter of Anil's mother is Anil's sister; since she is Rani's mother, Anil is Rani's maternal uncle.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If 1 January 2025 was a Wednesday, what day of the week was 15 August 2025?
questions.e: Count the odd days between the two dates: 226 days = 32 weeks and 2 odd day(s), so the weekday shifts by 2 from Wednesday to Friday.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: 2024 was a leap year and 29 February 2024 was a Thursday. What day was 25 December 2024?
questions.e: Count the odd days between the two dates: 300 days = 42 weeks and 6 odd day(s), so the weekday shifts by 6 from Thursday to Wednesday.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If 26 January 2026 is a Monday, what day of the week is 2 October 2026?
questions.e: Count the odd days between the two dates: 249 days = 35 weeks and 4 odd day(s), so the weekday shifts by 4 from Monday to Friday.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If 8 March 2025 was a Saturday, what day of the week was 14 November 2025?
questions.e: Count the odd days between the two dates: 251 days = 35 weeks and 6 odd day(s), so the weekday shifts by 6 from Saturday to Friday.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: At 3:15, what angle do the hour hand and the minute hand make with each other?

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 6 o'clock.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: When a clock shows 9:30, through what angle are the hour and minute hands separated?

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Calculate the angle between the two hands of a clock showing 12:10.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a row of 40 students, Ravi is 12th from the left end. What is his position from the right end?
questions.e: Position from the right = total − position from left + 1 = 40 − 12 + 1 = 29th.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Sita stands 7th from the front and 15th from the back in a queue. How many people are in the queue?
questions.e: Total = position from front + position from back − 1 = 7 + 15 − 1 = 21.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a row of 50 children, Mohan is 18th from the right end. What is his rank from the left end?
questions.e: Rank from the left = total − rank from right + 1 = 50 − 18 + 1 = 33rd.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Rahul is 9th from the left, Priya is 6th from the right, and 4 students stand between them. How many students are in the row?
questions.e: Total = 9 + 6 + 4 = 19 students.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Given that 5 − 3 gives 16 and 7 − 2 gives 45, what does 9 − 4 give?
questions.e: The rule is a² − b²: 25 − 9 = 16 and 49 − 4 = 45, so 81 − 16 = 65.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a certain code, 4 × 3 is written as 25 and 6 × 2 is written as 40. How would 5 × 5 be written?
questions.e: The code computes a² + b²: 16 + 9 = 25 and 36 + 4 = 40, so 5 × 5 becomes 25 + 25 = 50.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Study the pattern: 8 ÷ 2 → 12, 12 ÷ 3 → 16. What does 20 ÷ 4 become?
questions.e: Each result is a + 2b: 8 + 4 = 12 and 12 + 4 = 16, so 20 ÷ 4 becomes 20 + 4 = 24.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Complete the series analogy: (2, 3) → 13; (4, 1) → 17; (5, 2) → ?
questions.e: The mapping is a² + b²: 4 + 9 = 13 and 16 + 1 = 17, so (5, 2) maps to 25 + 4 = 29.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The approximate value of acceleration due to gravity (g) on the Earth's surface is:
questions.e: The standard value of g at the Earth's surface is 9.8 metres per second squared; it varies slightly with latitude and altitude.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The weight of a body at the centre of the Earth is:
o: equal to its weight at the surface
questions.e: At the Earth's centre the gravitational acceleration g is zero, so the weight (mass × g) of any body there is zero even though its mass is unchanged.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the Earth's mass were doubled and its radius halved, the acceleration due to gravity g would become:
questions.e: Since g = GM/R², doubling the mass multiplies g by 2 and halving the radius multiplies it by 2² = 4; together g becomes 2 × 4 = 8 times its original value.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the distance between two bodies is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes:
questions.e: Newton's law of gravitation is an inverse-square law: doubling the separation r makes the force F proportional to 1/(2r)² = 1/4 of the original.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity on the Moon's surface is about:
questions.e: The Moon's gravity is roughly one-sixth of Earth's, about 1.6 m/s², which is why astronauts could take long bounding strides there.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The SI unit of pressure is:
questions.e: Pressure is force per unit area; its SI unit is the newton per square metre, named the pascal after Blaise Pascal.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One bar of pressure is equal to:
questions.e: The bar is defined as exactly 100,000 pascals, close to standard atmospheric pressure at sea level.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Standard atmospheric pressure at sea level is approximately:
questions.e: One standard atmosphere equals 1.01325 × 10⁵ pascals, about 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa, the weight of the air column above sea level.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A sharp knife cuts better than a blunt one because:
o: it applies greater pressure on a smaller area
questions.e: Pressure equals force divided by area. A sharper edge concentrates the same force on a much smaller area, producing far greater pressure.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Dams are built thicker at the base than at the top because:
o: water is denser at the bottom
questions.e: Pressure in a liquid grows as hρg with depth h, so the deepest part of a dam faces the greatest water pressure and needs the thickest wall.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The SI unit of magnetic flux density (magnetic field strength) is:
questions.e: Magnetic flux density B is measured in teslas in the SI system; one tesla equals one weber per square metre.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A freely suspended bar magnet comes to rest pointing in the:
questions.e: The Earth's magnetic field pulls the magnet's north pole toward magnetic north, so a free magnet settles along the north–south line.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The space around a magnet in which its magnetic influence can be detected is called the:
questions.e: The magnetic field is the region surrounding a magnet where a compass needle or iron filing experiences a magnetic force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following materials is strongly attracted by a magnet?
questions.e: Iron is ferromagnetic and is strongly attracted to magnets, while copper, aluminium and wood show no such attraction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Outside a bar magnet, the magnetic lines of force travel:
o: from the south pole to the north pole
from the north pole to the south pole
questions.e: By convention, magnetic field lines emerge from the north pole, loop through the surrounding space, and re-enter at the south pole.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The SI unit of electric current is the:
questions.e: Electric current — the rate of flow of charge — is measured in amperes, one of the seven SI base units.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The SI unit of luminous intensity is the:
questions.e: Luminous intensity, the brightness of a light source in a given direction, has the SI base unit candela.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following is a derived SI unit?
questions.e: The metre, kilogram and second are base SI units; the newton (kg·m/s²) is derived from them.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The SI unit of frequency is the:
questions.e: Frequency counts cycles per second; its SI unit is the hertz, so a 50 Hz supply completes 50 cycles each second.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The SI unit of electric charge is the:
questions.e: Electric charge is measured in coulombs; one ampere of current delivers one coulomb of charge per second.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The rate of change of velocity of a body is called:
questions.e: Acceleration is defined as the change in velocity per unit time, measured in m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body moving in uniform circular motion has:
questions.e: The speed stays constant but the direction of velocity keeps changing, so the body is continuously accelerated toward the centre.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Newton's second law of motion relates:
questions.e: The second law states F = ma — the force on a body equals its mass times its acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If no external force acts on a moving body, it will:
questions.e: With zero net force there is zero acceleration, so by Newton's first law the body maintains whatever velocity it already had.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The distance–time graph of a body moving with uniform speed is:
questions.e: With uniform speed, distance grows in direct proportion to time, so the distance–time graph is a straight line through the origin.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Diamond and graphite are allotropes of:
questions.e: Allotropes are different structural forms of the same element; diamond and graphite are both pure carbon arranged differently.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The hardest naturally occurring substance known is:
questions.e: Diamond's rigid tetrahedral carbon lattice gives it the maximum hardness of 10 on the Mohs scale.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Diamond is the hardest known natural substance because its carbon atoms:
o: are arranged in layers that slide easily
form a rigid three-dimensional tetrahedral network of covalent bonds
share electrons freely like a metal
questions.e: In diamond every carbon atom is tetrahedrally bonded to four others in a continuous 3D covalent lattice, which makes it extremely hard.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A molecule of buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀) contains:
questions.e: Buckminsterfullerene is a hollow cage of carbon atoms arranged like a football, containing exactly 60 carbon atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The valency of carbon in its compounds is:
questions.e: Carbon has four electrons in its outer shell and typically shares all four, giving it a valency of 4 as seen in methane (CH₄).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The burning of magnesium ribbon in air is an example of a:
questions.e: Magnesium combines directly with oxygen (2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO) with a dazzling white flame — two reactants forming one product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When an acid reacts with a base, the products formed are:
questions.e: Acid–base neutralisation always yields a salt plus water, for example HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An oxide that reacts with both acids and bases is called:
questions.e: Amphoteric oxides such as zinc oxide and aluminium oxide react with both acids and bases to form salts and water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a displacement reaction, a more reactive metal:
o: displaces a less reactive metal from its compound
is displaced by a less reactive metal
questions.e: The reactivity series rules displacement: for example, zinc displaces copper from copper sulphate because zinc is more reactive.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Photosynthesis in green plants is an example of an:
questions.e: Photosynthesis absorbs light energy to build glucose from carbon dioxide and water, so it is endothermic — energy is taken in, not released.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The Haber process manufactures ammonia from:
questions.e: In the Haber process, nitrogen and hydrogen combine (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃) over an iron catalyst at high pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The Contact process is used in the industrial manufacture of:
questions.e: The Contact process oxidises sulphur dioxide to sulphur trioxide over a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst to make sulphuric acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The main raw materials for the Solvay process (manufacture of sodium carbonate) are:
questions.e: The Solvay process reacts sodium chloride brine with ammonia and carbon dioxide from limestone to produce washing soda.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Cast iron contains approximately what percentage of carbon?
questions.e: Cast iron is an iron–carbon alloy with roughly 2–4% carbon, which makes it hard and brittle compared with steel.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Stainless steel resists rusting mainly because it contains:
questions.e: Chromium (at least about 10.5%) forms a thin protective oxide layer on the surface, which is what makes stainless steel stainless.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The digestion of starch begins in the:
questions.e: Salivary amylase in saliva starts breaking starch into sugars right in the mouth during chewing.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The largest gland in the human body is the:
questions.e: The liver is the largest internal gland; it produces bile, processes nutrients and detoxifies blood.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The digestion of starch begins in the mouth with the help of the enzyme:
questions.e: Salivary amylase starts breaking starch into maltose in the mouth; pepsin digests proteins, trypsin acts in the small intestine and lipase digests fats.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The digestion of proteins begins in the:
questions.e: The stomach's pepsin enzyme, working in acidic gastric juice, begins breaking proteins into peptides.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The absorption of digested food takes place mainly in the:
questions.e: The small intestine's folded walls carry millions of villi that absorb digested nutrients into the blood.

questions.subject: Railway GK
questions.q: On railway curves, the outer rail is raised (superelevation or cant) mainly to:
o: counteract centrifugal force on the train
reduce the weight of the rails
increase friction between wheels and rails
questions.e: Raising the outer rail tilts the train inward so a component of its weight balances the centrifugal force on curves, reducing derailment risk.

questions.subject: Railway GK
questions.q: Indian Railways' electrified routes run on:
questions.e: India uses a 25,000-volt alternating-current overhead system at 50 Hz for its electrified broad-gauge network.

questions.subject: Railway GK
questions.q: The device on an electric locomotive that collects current from the overhead wire is the:
questions.e: The pantograph is the jointed, spring-loaded arm on the locomotive roof that slides along the overhead catenary wire.

questions.subject: Railway GK
questions.q: A small gap is left between successive rails to allow for:
questions.e: Steel rails expand in heat; the expansion gap prevents the track from buckling when temperatures rise.

questions.subject: Railway GK
questions.q: In the locomotive class 'WAP-7', the letter 'P' stands for:
questions.e: In Indian locomotive codes, W = broad gauge, A = AC electric, and P = passenger (as against G for goods).

questions.subject: Railway GK
questions.q: 'Kavach', developed for Indian Railways, is:
questions.e: Kavach is India's indigenous automatic train protection system, designed to prevent collisions by automatically applying brakes.

questions.subject: Railway GK
questions.q: India's longest railway tunnel is:
o: Tunnel T-49 on the USBRL Katra–Banihal section
questions.e: Tunnel T-49 (about 12.76 km) on the Udhampur–Srinagar–Baramulla link overtook the 11.2 km Pir Panjal tunnel as India's longest rail tunnel.

questions.subject: Railway GK
questions.q: The Pir Panjal railway tunnel (11.2 km) lies on the:
questions.e: The 11.2 km Pir Panjal tunnel carries the railway between Banihal and Qazigund in Jammu & Kashmir.

questions.subject: Railway GK
questions.q: The longest tunnel on the Konkan Railway is the:
questions.e: The 6.5 km Karbude Tunnel between Ukshi and Bhoke is the longest of the 90-plus tunnels on the Konkan Railway.

questions.subject: Railway GK
questions.q: Railway tunnels are given a concrete lining mainly to:
o: reduce the noise of passing trains
hold the overhead electric wires in place
support the rock face and prevent water seepage
questions.e: The lining supports the excavated rock face, stops loose rock from falling and seals the tunnel against groundwater seepage.

questions.subject: Railway GK
questions.q: Tunnel T-49 was built using the:
questions.e: Engineers used the New Austrian Tunnelling Method — a drill-and-blast technique suited to the fragile Himalayan rock of the USBRL section.

questions.subject: Railway GK
questions.q: India's first metro railway started operations in:
questions.e: The Kolkata Metro began on 24 October 1984 between Esplanade and Bhowanipur — India's first metro and first underground railway.

questions.subject: Railway GK
questions.q: The first corridor of the Delhi Metro (Shahdara–Tis Hazari) opened in:

capsules.subject: Recruitment
capsules.title: RRB NTPC Graduate (CEN 06/2026): 3,548 posts; apply by 6 November 2026
capsules.body: The Railway Recruitment Boards have opened applications for RRB NTPC Graduate Recruitment 2026 (CEN 06/2026) — 3,548 posts for Chief Commercial-cum-Ticket Supervisor (127), Goods Train Manager (2,750), Junior Accounts Assistant-cum-Typist (300) and Senior Clerk-cum-Typist (371). Apply online 8 October – 6 November 2026 (11:59 PM) at rrb.indianrailways.gov.in; fee by 8 November, correction window 9–18 November. Eligibility: bachelor’s degree; age 18–33 as on 01.01.2027. Fee: ₹500 (UR/OBC/EWS), ₹250 (SC/ST/female/ESM/Minorities/EBC/PwBD). Selection: CBT-1 → CBT-2 → document verification/medical. Notable: the CBT-based Typing Skill Test has been dispensed with for CEN 06/2026; negative marking 1/3; apply to only one RRB; initial pay ₹29,200–₹35,400.

Together with the graduate-level CEN 06/2026 (3,548 posts, deadline 6 November), the Railways’ NTPC recruitment this season covers 5,236 posts. Candidates must read the official CEN notifications on rrb.indianrailways.gov.in for post-wise eligibility, medical standards and reservation rules before applying.
